title: introduce-economic-fallthrough-engine-and-quant-cohort-linter
author: Ethan Liu
release_notes: Add Economic Fallthrough Engine to route eligible requests to cheaper quantized model variants under unit-econ guarantees; include Quant Cohort Linter to validate quant profile consistency; introduce workload cohort defaults for batching and KV cache. Rollout with canary and metrics guardrails.
description:
Summary: This PR adds two related pieces of automation for cost optimization: 1) an Economic Fallthrough Engine (EFE) that makes request-level routing decisions to fall back to cheaper quantized model variants when unit economy checks indicate acceptable risk, and 2) a Quant Cohort Linter that statically and dynamically flags inconsistent quantization profiles across model cohorts.
Motivation: Customers want predictable unit economics without regressing quality. We frequently see manual ad-hoc fallbacks that either regress accuracy or fail to capture cost wins. EFE codifies a conservative policy allowing safe fallthrough to smaller/quantized variants when workload signatures and eval-driven thresholds are satisfied.
Design:
- EFE evaluates three signals at request time: workload cohort, live quality estimate (fast embedding similarity + sketch of rerank delta), and unit-econ delta (expected tokens * cost-per-token delta). The policy DSL supports hard thresholds (e.g. max-allowed-quality-delta) and soft gates (budget-weighted scoring).
- Quant Cohort Linter runs on model manifests and CI to detect mismatched quant settings (e.g. a 4-bit profile missing KV cache-friendly layout), and flags runtime incompatibilities that would make fallthrough unsafe.
- Batch/cache defaults: Introduce cohort-aware defaults for batching (target_microbatch / preferred_batch_window_ms) and KV cache retention. These defaults are conservative; they can be overridden per-tenant.
Implementation:
- runtime/fallthrough/engine.go: core policy evaluation + metrics hooks.
- runtime/fallthrough/policy_dsl.go: small DSL with unit-econ expressions and fallthrough scoring.
- optimizer/quant/linter.py: static validators + dynamic test harness to replay small batches and check output distributions.
- infra/telemetry/metrics.yaml: new metrics (econ_fallthrough_attempts, econ_fallthrough_accepts, quant_linter_issues) and dashboard templates.
- docs/operational/econ-fallthrough.md: design doc, rollout playbook, rollback steps, and example policy snippets.
Safety & mitigations:
- Conservative defaults: EFE is off by default for tenants; it can be enabled via tenant feature flag.
- Canary rollout plan below: start at 1% traffic, monitor quality delta and fallback ratio, escalate to 5/25/100% only on green.
- Automatic auto-revert if sliding-window quality regression > 0.75% or if error rate increases by > 0.5% over baseline.
Testing:
- unit tests for policy evaluation and DSL parsing.
- integration test that runs 500 synthetic requests across synthetic cohorts to assert that fallthrough occurs only when unit-econ delta > threshold and quality proxies are within tolerance.
- CI harness runs the Quant Cohort Linter against the model registry (snapshot) and fails if new models introduce incompatible quant layouts.
Measured results from internal experiment (toy tenant):
- Average per-token cost reduction for targeted baseline: 8.3%
- Median latency change: +7ms (within SLA)
- Quality proxy regression (similarity sketch): 0.3% (below threshold)
Rollout plan:
1) Enable EFE in staging + run linter for entire model catalog.
2) Canary 1% of traffic (48h) -> 5% (72h) -> 25% (7d) -> 100% if no regressions.
3) Expose safe-config presets via Console and a dry-run mode that logs potential savings without applying fallthroughs.
Related work items: Linear ENG-784 (fallthrough engine prototype), ENG-810 (quant linting + CI).
Checklist:
- [x] Core runtime + policy DSL
- [x] Quant Cohort Linter + CI integration
- [x] Metrics + dashboards
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Docs and rollout playbook
- [x] Feature flag gating for tenants

review_conversation:
Priya Desai: Can you walk through how cohort identification works for traffic with mixed patterns?
Ethan Liu: Cohorts are generated by sampling recent requests and clustering on short signatures (prompt length, prompt embedding centroid, route). We use a sliding window to adapt.
Miguel Santos: Linter flagged two registry entries with incompatible KV layouts; are we auto-blocking publish?
Ethan Liu: Linter fails CI by default for protected branches; for model-publish pipeline we added a suppressible warning mode for experimental channels.
Harriet Cole: Suggest adding a flag to make the canary duration configurable as a tenant-level policy.
Ethan Liu: Added tenant.canary.duration in config/defaults/cohort-batch-presets.yaml and added docs.
Priya Desai: Two minor nits on logging verbosity in engine.go.
Ethan Liu: Addressed (removed noisy debug logs behind feature flag).
Miguel Santos: CI flakes on the quant-linter job intermittently; can we add retry?
Ethan Liu: Added 3x retry on transient linter jobs and hardened an environment var.
Approved-by: Priya Desai, Miguel Santos

notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: feature is gated and requires tenant opt-in. Operators should follow docs/operational/econ-fallthrough.md for rollback and emergency kill-switch procedures. The quant cohort linter has been turned on in protected-branch CI; teams introducing experimental quant profiles should run linter in dry-run mode first.
